title: Routing rule schema and rollout playbook (notes)
content:
Purpose and context:

This is a working note for the routing rule configuration schema, validator rules, and rollout mechanics we want the Redwood control plane to enforce. Goal: produce a compact, machine-parseable schema that supports our multi-region routing, tiering (hosted/dedicated/private), fallbacks, and canary rollouts without requiring custom per-customer code.

Scope (what this doc contains):
- JSON/YAML schema sketch for routing rules
- Validation guidelines (static and runtime)
- Rollout mechanics / canary semantics and automated checks
- Test cases and CI gates for rule changes
- Open questions / TODOs

High-level design constraints:
- Declarative: rules are declarative objects stored in control plane (config DB) and validated before activation.
- Deterministic routing: given incoming request metadata and rule set version, routing decision must be deterministic.
- Fast-evaluating: policies used in hot path should evaluate in <500us median.
- Safe rollouts: control plane supports staged activations with automated health/fallback.
- Multi-region aware: can target region(s) and include cross-region fallback with latency/cost constraints.

Minimal routing rule primitives (v0):
- selector: match criteria over request attributes (model, customer_id, region, latency_tier, route_name)
- priority: integer (higher wins)
- action: one of {route, split, failover, transform, deny} (route = target model variant or endpoint pool)
- targets: list of candidate endpoints/model variants with weights (for split/canary)
- constraints: optional soft/hard constraints (max_latency_ms, max_cost_per_token, allowed_tiers)
- rollout: rollout policy metadata (start_time, end_time, steps)
- id + version + metadata (owner, changelist)

Example YAML (user-facing editing format):

# --- routing-rule-v0 ---
# Matches all requests for model "llama-70b" from EU and routes to dedicated pool A with canary split
- id: rule-llama-eu-dedicated
  version: "2026-02-01"
  priority: 100
  selector:
    model: "llama-70b"
    regions: ["eu-west-1", "eu-central-1"]
    customer_tier: ["enterprise", "dedicated_contract"]
  action: split
  targets:
    - endpoint: "dedicated-eu-pool-A"
      weight: 90
    - endpoint: "dedicated-eu-canary-1"
      weight: 10
  constraints:
    max_latency_ms: 150
    allowed_tiers: ["dedicated", "hosted_fallback"]
  rollout:
    mode: progressive
    steps:
      - pct: 10
        duration_minutes: 60
      - pct: 50
        duration_minutes: 30
      - pct: 100
        duration_minutes: 0
  metadata:
    created_by: "asha@redwood.ai"
    notes: "initial canary for dedicated EU pool"

Validation rules (static pre-activation checks):
- Syntax: YAML parses to allowed schema fields. Unknown top-level fields fail with `error: unknown_field` unless flagged as `experimental:true`.
- Selector sanity: selectors must contain at least one dimension (model or route_name or customer_id). Empty selector is forbidden.
- Priority: 0-1000 integer range. Deduplicate rule ids per namespace.
- Targets: sum(weights) must be >0. Each referenced endpoint must exist in endpoint registry and be compatible (model architecture + quantization).
- Constraints: hard constraints (e.g., allowed_tiers) that cannot be guaranteed by control plane are allowed but require `acknowledge_risk:true` to activate.
- Rollout semantics: progressive mode requires explicit steps with pct increasing to 100. Instant mode can be used but must have `force:true` and an owner/justification.

Runtime validation / safety checks (activated during rollout):
- Endpoint health: before increasing pct to next step, ensure target endpoints have healthy=TRUE for N consecutive checks (default N=3).
- Latency/cost guardrails: if median latency > constraints.max_latency_ms by >25% for the last evaluation window, pause/rollback.
- Error rate: if 5xx rate increases by >50% relative to baseline for the route_name in the same window, pause and roll back to previous stable config.
- Fallback activation: when all targets in a rule are unhealthy, automatically switch to configured failover rule (if present) or fallback endpoints tagged `hosted_fallback`.

Rollout mechanic details (control plane responsibilities):
1) Pre-commit checks in PR: schema validation, unit tests for new rule behavior (simulator), endpoint compatibility checks (registry queries). CI gate: no rule merge if any blocking validator fails.
2) Staged activation: when an update is submitted to the control plane, it enters a staging namespace and is applied as `staged_version`.
3) Canary window: control plane drives traffic according to rollout.steps, measuring health metrics from observability pipeline (latency, errors, qps, token-cost).
4) Automated decisioning: each step has pass/fail criteria (defaults below). If pass, continue; if fail, auto-rollback to previous stable version and alert owners.
5) Manual override: SRE/owner can abort/force_continue via console or API with `reason` logged.

Default step pass criteria (configurable global policy):
- min_samples: 200 requests to the canary target in the step window OR duration_minutes elapsed (whichever later).
- latency_threshold_pct: 20% (canary median latency must not exceed baseline median by >20%)
- error_increase_pct: 30%
- cost_delta_pct: 50% (if unit cost increases too much, fail)

Testing & CI:
- Unit tests: router simulator that replays sample traffic and asserts target weighting and determinism. Include edge cases: overlapping selectors, exact priority tie-breakers.
- Integration tests: deploy rule to a sandbox control plane with synthetic endpoints (healthy/unhealthy) and validate rollout behavior, failover paths.
- Fuzz tests: generate malformed selectors and unusual weight distributions to ensure validator rejects unsafe rules.
- Production shadowing: new validator changes must run in shadow mode against production configs for 72 hours before being allowed to block activations.

Examples of tricky scenarios and our intended behavior:
- Overlapping rules: rules are evaluated in priority order (higher priority first). If selectors are identical and priority ties, tie-breaker = last_modified timestamp (newer wins) — this reduces surprising precedence flips but must be audited.
- Cross-region latency-aware failover: rule prefers in-region endpoints; if in-region median latency > max_latency_ms, control plane may route to nearest-region fallback if within cost bounds.
- Model variant compatibility: control plane must reject routing to an endpoint whose model.size > request.max_allowed_size (enforced by endpoint registry metadata).

Operational runbook (short):
- Rule activation alerts: on failure during rollout, alerting channel #plat-routing and paging to on-call SRE.
- Quick rollback: control plane supports `activate_version(rule_id, target_version=previous)` API for instant revert.
- Emergency global deny: `global-route-disable` config to short-circuit all routing in worst-case (manual guard with 2-person auth).

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should selectors support boolean logic (AND/OR/NOT) or only lists of values? (Pros: expressive. Cons: evaluation complexity and potential slowness.)
- Authorization model: which roles can create `force:true` instant activations? Propose: only platform-admin + owner.
- Audit retention: store full pre-activation diffs for 90 days.
- Schema versioning strategy: add `schema_version` top-level and compatibility tests in validator.

Immediate next steps (owners):
- Asha: draft formal JSON Schema file and add to platform repo (PR target: platform/schemas/routing-rule-v0.json) — due 2026-02-21.
- Diego: implement pre-commit validator hook that queries endpoint registry (PR #938) — due 2026-03-04.
- Sofia: build router simulator unit tests and include example traffic sets for EU/US/ROW — due 2026-03-07.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally pragmatic: start with restricted, well-validated primitives. We can add expression language later once we have telemetry and confidence.
- Please annotate big design concerns inline in the PR rather than in comments here.

End of note.
